questions.q: What is the main difference between prompt engineering and context engineering?
options: Prompt engineering crafts one instruction; context engineering decides what else surrounds it in the window
Context engineering only applies to image models, not text models
They are two names for exactly the same task
Prompt engineering is done by the model, context engineering by the developer
questions.explain: Prompt engineering is about wording a single instruction well; context engineering is about everything else sent alongside it — system prompt, tools, history, retrieval.

questions.q: In the example call (system 1,400 / tools 2,600 / history 5,100 / retrieved 3,800 / user prompt 40 tokens), what does the user's literal prompt represent?
options: Most of the total tokens sent
Exactly half of the total tokens sent
A small fraction of the total tokens actually sent to the model
The only thing the model is allowed to use
questions.explain: 40 tokens out of nearly 13,000 total — the literal prompt is a small fraction of what's actually in the context window.

questions.q: Why did context engineering become a distinct discipline as systems grew more agentic?
options: Because models stopped reading system prompts
Because assembled context (history, tools, retrieval) came to dwarf the user's own words once multi-turn and tool-using systems became common
Because token limits were removed entirely
Because prompt engineering is no longer needed at all
questions.explain: In single-turn Q&A, the prompt's wording dominated. With multi-turn, tool use, and retrieval, the surrounding context became the larger and more failure-prone part of the window.

questions.q: A response comes back wrong. What does this lesson say you should ask first?
options: Whether to switch to a different model entirely
Whether the user typed their question correctly
Nothing — always reword the prompt first regardless of cause
Whether the instruction itself was unclear, or whether it was clear but buried under irrelevant context
questions.explain: The lesson's core practical point: distinguishing a prompt problem from a context problem determines which fix actually addresses the cause.

questions.q: Which of these is a context-engineering decision rather than a prompt-engineering one?
options: Deciding how many prior conversation turns to include in this call
Choosing whether to phrase an instruction as a question or a command
Picking the exact wording of a single few-shot example
Choosing between present-tense and past-tense phrasing in an instruction
questions.explain: How much history to include is about what surrounds the instruction in the window — a context-engineering decision, not a wording decision.
